newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury to lose Whitehall address in revamp.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury to lose Whitehall address in revamp.

text.p: The Treasury will lose its prestigious address in Whitehall, the heart of Britain's government district, under plans to redevelop its main building announced on Thursday.

The developers of the building, Exchequer Partnership Plc, intend to build a hotel and/or offices at the western, Whitehall end of the building, Financial Secretary Michael Jack said in a written parliamentary answer.

Flats will probably be built at the eastern end overlooking St James's Park, leaving the Treasury sandwiched in the remaining middle third of the building. The new main entrance would be on the south side of the building on St George Street.

The present timetable, subject to planning permission, calls for Treasury staff to vacate the building in autumn 1998 -- they will move temporarily to Vauxhall, south of the river Thames -- and reoccupy part of it in mid-2001.
The building is being modernised behind its existing facade under the umbrella of the government's private finance initiative.

Commercial Heads of Terms have been agreed, marking a significant milestone in the negotiation process and enabling the Treasury and Exchequer Partnership to proceed with the project in principle, subject to final contract, Jack said.
